insights.title: SAP RPT1 — +0.37 pts MoM
insights.body: SAP-RPT-1 is a genuinely new kind of model, pretrained on business tables so it can predict things like late payments or won deals without anyone training a model first, and it moved from TechEd announcement in November 2025 to purchasable service inside SAP AI Core by December 2025. Practitioner reaction is enthusiastic about the concept but the only independent benchmark available, published by a Microsoft engineer in February 2026, found it matches tuned gradient-boosted trees only on small classification problems and loses on regression and larger datasets. The visible evidence base is launch blogs, playground experiments and vendor material, with almost no named customer running it in production, so adoption and maturity must be scored low despite strong positive sentiment.
bullets: SAP's own launch blog from November 2025 drew 36,665 views and 90 likes but only six comments, a sign of curiosity rather than hands-on deployment.
By December 2025 both sap-rpt-1-small, with a 2,000-row context, and sap-rpt-1-large, with a 64,000-row context, were offered for productive use in SAP's generative AI hub.

insights.title: Business Data Cloud — +0.25 pts MoM
insights.body: Business Data Cloud is landing well with the people it was built for: SAP shops trying to get ERP data into analytics without copying it endlessly, where reviewers score it 8.6 out of 10 on TrustRadius across 83 ratings and 4.2 out of 5 on G2 across 76 reviews. The Databricks link is real rather than slideware, with SAP's business meanings for tables and columns now syncing automatically into Databricks governance, but practitioners are blunt that the product loses its point when the main source system is not SAP, and they complain about cost, developer troubleshooting and clunky interfaces. Evidence here is drawn mostly from review-site summaries and vendor or consultancy commentary, with no named chief data officers, so this read is directional rather than definitive.
bullets: TrustRadius records 8.6 out of 10 across 83 ratings and G2 4.2 out of 5 across 76 reviews, with zero one- or two-star scores but a still-small base.
Reviewers credit zero-copy federation, meaning data is queried where it lives instead of duplicated, as the feature that finally attacks SAP data silos while keeping business context.

insights.title: Joule AI Assistant — +0.12 pts MoM
insights.body: Joule has moved from a chat box bolted onto SAP screens to a broader agent platform, with Joule Studio for building custom agents reaching general availability in early 2026 and prebuilt agents shipping for finance, supply chain and HR. The evidence available here is heavily weighted towards SAP marketing and partner commentary rather than independent user reviews: the concrete practitioner signals that do exist are about cost unpredictability from metered AI units, dependence on clean master data, immature custom-agent tooling, and support tickets where Joule simply refuses a request. Because none of the supplied pages contain Reddit threads, G2 or Gartner Peer Insights ratings, or named customers quantifying benefit, satisfaction and real adoption depth are read cautiously and confidence is low.
bullets: SAP's 2026 Sapphire pitch claims more than 50 domain-specific Joule Assistants orchestrating over 200 agents, a scale claim no customer evidence on these pages verifies.
An independent ERP buyer guide reviewed in July 2026 warns that SAP's own Joule material is promotional and most third-party coverage comes from partners with an interest in the answer.

insights.title: The market is the story, not any one model
insights.body: Total routed tokens reached 735.6T (+40% month-to-date vs the same weeks of Oct '26). As the pie grew, share moved toward lower-cost and open-weight models — Tencent (+14.7pp), DeepSeek (+3.7pp) gained, while Xiaomi (-5.8pp), Z.ai (-3.7pp), StepFun (-2.0pp) gave up ground. A falling share here can sit on top of flat or only slightly lower volume.

insights.title: Gemini in context — it didn’t go to zero
insights.body: OpenRouter measures one slice (developer API routing, cost-sensitive). On the slices that track Google’s actual business, Gemini is strong — the share drop here is a routing story, not a collapse.
bullets: OpenRouter developer tokens: Google share 3.8% → 3.1% (-0.7pp), 23.1T routed — down, but far from gone.
Top Gemini model on OpenRouter: Gemini 4 Carbon 1110, ranked #18 by tokens.
Alphabet Q3 2026: search revenue +12% YoY, total revenue $127.6B (+25% YoY).
